preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is between 2 and 400 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(abs(x) <= 1000 and abs(y) <= 1000 for x, y in points)
preconditions.description: All node coordinates (x, y) have absolute values at most 1000.
There are exactly n distinct points provided.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' if not exists_valid_tree else stdout.strip() != '-1' and abs(float(stdout.strip()) - min_total_length) <= 1e-6 * max(1.0, abs(min_total_length))
postconditions.description: If no valid binary root tree exists where every arc goes from a higher y-coordinate to a lower y-coordinate, output -1. Otherwise, output the minimum total arc length with required precision.

postconditions.expression: exists_valid_tree == (any(all(y_parent > y_child for y_parent, y_child in zip(parents, children)) and all(out_degree <= 2 for out_degree in out_degrees) and is_connected_tree(parents, children, n) for parents, children, out_degrees in all_possible_binary_trees(points)))
postconditions.description: A valid tree exists if and only if there is a configuration of arcs forming a binary tree (max 2 outgoing arcs per node) rooted at some node, where every arc connects a node with a strictly greater y-coordinate to one with a strictly smaller y-coordinate, and the graph is connected with exactly one path from the root to every other node.

postconditions.expression: min_total_length == min(sum((x1-x2)**2 + (y1-y2)**2 for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in arcs) ** 0.5 for arcs in all_valid_binary_trees_arcs(points)) if exists_valid_tree else 0.0
postconditions.description: The minimum total length is the sum of Euclidean distances of all arcs in the valid binary tree configuration that minimizes this sum.
